reason: The text depicts the Hebrew people actively expressing their views directly to King Rehoboam. Multiple instances show them speaking their concerns: they approach Rehoboam collectively and request relief from Solomon's heavy labor (וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֖ם), and later when the king refuses to listen, they openly express their dissent and rebellion (מַה־ לָּנוּ֩ חֵ֨לֶק בְּדָוִ֜ד). Rather than being discouraged from expressing their views, the people are portrayed as freely voicing their grievances and political position. The issue presented in the text is not suppression of speech but the king's refusal to hear and respond favorably to what they express.
